Water-quality safety thresholds (this page's method, formula-based rather than lookup): NH₄⁺ dissociation pKa = 9.25 − 0.031 × (water temp − 25) (temperature correction); unionized ammonia fraction = 1 ÷ (1 + 10^(pKa − pH)); measured NH₃ = total ammonia nitrogen TAN × fraction; TAN safe limit = 0.02 ÷ fraction (back-calculated from the 0.02 mg/L NH₃ threshold); nitrite safe limit = min(0.1, chloride × 0.0132) (estimated from Cl⁻÷NO₂⁻-N molar ratio ≥30, with 0.1 mg/L as absolute ceiling). Validation: water temp 0–40 °C, pH 6–10, chloride must be a valid number >0 (otherwise nitrite limit cannot be estimated), TAN/nitrite must be valid ≥0; empty or out-of-range inputs prompt and abort (clearing prior results). Criteria: NH₃<0.02 safe, ≥0.02 exceeds limit (≥0.05 severe); NO₂⁻-N ≤ limit safe, > limit exceeds.

Common pairs: 3.9 mmol/L ≈ 70 mg/dL (lower normal limit and hypoglycemia alert), 5.6 ≈ 100.9, 6.1 ≈ 110 (upper fasting normal), 7.0 ≈ 126.1 (fasting diabetes diagnostic threshold), 7.8 ≈ 140 (2-hour postprandial upper normal), 11.1 ≈ 200.0 (random with symptoms diabetes threshold).

Random glucose 11.1 mmol/L → × 18.0182 ≈ 200.0 mg/dL, reaching the random diabetes diagnostic threshold. Reverse: meter shows 100.9 mg/dL → ÷ 18.0182 ≈ 5.60 mmol/L. This tool consistently uses 18.0182: option coefficients are based on mmol/L (mmol/L = 18.0182, mg/dL = 1), output = input × source coefficient ÷ target coefficient; the default is "mmol/L → mg/dL", showing the common 5.6 → 100.9 conversion on load.

Criterion: larger MTBF means longer average trouble-free operation; λ is its reciprocal.
